text:
jenna: Heads up — benefits vendor notified us of a plan admin migration on 2025-04-15 with a 48-hour blackout window. Will this pause 401(k) loan repayments or payroll deferrals? Need to let eng teams. @payroll

alex_hr: Thanks for flagging. Do we have exact start/end times from vendor? That determines payroll timing impact.

maria_benefits: Vendor sent: 'Migration begins 2025-04-15 22:00 UTC, expected completion 2025-04-17 22:00 UTC.' They said transactions submitted before window should process as usual; anything queued during will be delayed. cc @sam_payroll

sam_payroll: :thinking_face: If migration overlaps our pay run cutoff (04/16 05:00 PT) then deferrals recorded on that day might be pending. Loan repayments are usually handled as post-tax deductions via vendor — might be delayed one cycle. I'll check payroll feed.

ben: If repayments are delayed will that count as missed loan payment? Employees will freak. Any grace?

maria_benefits: Vendor guaranteed no missed-loan penalties; they'll backdate repayments. But employees won't see deduction until processed — they'll get a message. We should craft comms.

alex_hr: Can we shift the payroll cutoff for that pay run earlier by 12 hours? Sam?

sam_payroll: We can shift, but needs approval. Shifting cutoff means we must close adjustments earlier. Ops can do it if leadership signs off.

jenna: Also quick Q: if someone changes deferral allocation (Traditional -> Roth) the vendor said the change effective date is the next payroll processed after their request. Will the blackout change effective date?

maria_benefits: Yes, changes submitted during blackout will be queued and effective on the next processed payroll after migration completes. So effective date could be later. We'll include that in the comms.

alex_hr: Action items: 1) Confirm with vendor in writing no loan penalties, 2) Decide payroll cutoff shift, 3) Draft employee note w/FAQ. I'll own comms. @jenna please help with timing.

jenna: I'll draft a short notice with bullets + FAQ. Any required language re: HSA/FSA? People ask about pretax elections.

maria_benefits: Mention HSA/FSA elections: contributions funded via payroll so same rules — changes during blackout delayed. Also auto-enrollment and catch-up contributions unaffected unless they coincide with blackout.

sam_payroll: I'll run a test of payroll feed submission tomorrow to see vendor behavior. If we need to shift cutoff I'll escalate.

hr-bot: Reminder: Submit any payroll cutoff requests at least 48 hours before desired change: https://intranet/payroll/operations :calendar: 

ben: Can we add a line on who to contact if they see an unexpected deduction? Preferably benefits@redwood.com

alex_hr: Yep. We'll route to benefits@redwood.com and payroll@redwood.com. Draft incoming within 24h.
